html:
The Curripaco, who call themselves Wakuenai, are an Arawakan people of the upper Rio Negro basin, along the Guainía, Isana and Inírida rivers where Colombia, Venezuela and Brazil meet. They are close kin of the Baniwa.

They farm bitter manioc, fish and hunt, and are known for basketry and for sacred flutes and trumpets used in men's rituals, linked to the myth of Kuwai. Portuguese slave raids up the Rio Negro hit the region in the 1700s, and rubber tappers in the late 1800s. From the late 1940s many converted to evangelical Protestantism through the work of the missionary Sophie Muller. Their neighbours include the Tukano peoples to the south.
